phase_evolution.value: κ-carbides precipitate and coarsen in the austenite during solution treatment; their size increases with carbon content, reaching ~50 nm for the 1.5%C (C-1.5) steel, the coarsest of the C series.

source.reason: For the 1.5%C steel the orientation relationship between κ-carbides and austenite was found to be (001)κ || (001)γ, and the interface is coherent (SAED evidence).

slip_behavior.value: Because the κ-carbides form a coherent interface with the austenite matrix, their strengthening contribution follows a particle shear model rather than an Orowan mechanism; particle shear strengthening is still active for κ-carbides as large as 50 nm. Shear deformation facilitates glide of dislocations across κ-carbide shear planes, weakening work hardening.

overall_structure.value: After solution treatment at 1050 °C for 2 h and water quenching the Fe30Mn11Al1.5C (C-1.5) steel is single-phase austenite (FCC) with uniformly distributed intragranular κ-carbide precipitates; no ferrite (BCC) phase is present in this composition (EBSD), unlike the 0.6%C steel. Austenite grains are coarse and contain abundant annealing twin boundaries; κ-carbides coarsen to the largest size of the C series.

source.reason: Combined EBSD and TEM characterization of the C-1.5 sample after 1050 °C/2 h solution treatment.

unmapped_findings: For C-1.5 (Fe30Mn11Al1.5C): σ_TS (maximum true stress just before necking, from UTS^a column) = 1343 MPa and fracture strength σ_FS (FRS^a column) = 1875 MPa (Table 2).
Charpy impact energy Akv-40 = 1.5 ± 0.2 J is the lowest impact toughness among all designed low-density steels, recorded for the Fe30Mn11Al1.5C steel (b0028, b0066).

Yield strength increased from 542 MPa (0.6%C) to 1125 MPa (1.5%C) while tensile elongation decreased from ~60% to ~20% with increasing carbon content (b0025); rapid work softening occurred in the 1.5%C steel.
Two different κ-carbide sizes are reported for the 1.5%C steel: ~80 nm average diameter from dark-field TEM (b0044) and 50 ± 18 nm in Table 3 (b0047).
Density of Fe30Mn11Al1.5C: measured 6.56 g/cm³ (Table 1); calculated from Eq. (3) as 6.55 g/cm³ (b0064).
Nominal/measured chemical composition of C-1.5: C 1.52, Mn 29.67, Al 11.21, Fe Bal. (mass%) (Table 1).

The paper's general models — density model ρ = 8.10 − 0.102C − 0.10Al − 0.01Mn (Eq. 3) and shear-strengthening model σ_shear = α f^1/2 d_Car^1/2 (Eq. 4), with yield-strength fit R_p0.2 = 478 + 97.1 d_Car^0.5 (MPa/nm^1/2) — are series-wide and not specific to the C-1.5 sample.
